request.system:
You are a workflow documentation expert.  You analyze sequences of screen observations and produce clear, actionable Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that another person or AI agent can follow to reproduce the same task.

Write SOPs that are:
- Specific: include exact URLs, field names, button labels, values
- Actionable: each step is a concrete action (click, type, navigate)
- Verified: each step includes how to confirm it worked
- Universal: use application names and locations, not DOM selectors

Respond with ONLY valid JSON.  No markdown fences, no commentary.

  "title": "Process and Submit Multi-Expense Travel and Meal Reports",
  "short_title": "Submit Expense Reports",
  "tags": ["finance", "browsing", "documentation"],
  "description": "This workflow aggregates scattered receipt data from Gmail into structured expense reports within Expensify, ensuring all travel and meal costs are documented and approved by the designated approver.",
  "outcome": "A complete, receipt-backed expense report is generated and submitted for financial approval.",
  "when_to_use": "When an employee needs to reconcile multiple receipts from email into a single or multiple expense reports for reimbursement.",

input: search_document: Upload receipts to expense report | This workflow aggregates scattered receipt data from Gmail into structured expense reports within Expensify, ensuring all travel and meal costs are documented and approved by the designated approver. | Search Gmail for receipts received since a specific date; Open a specific receipt email and download the PDF attachment; Create a new expense report in Expensify; Enter the first expense details (Merchant, Amount, Category, Date); Upload the corresponding receipt PDF as an attachment; Repeat steps 2 through 5 for additional receipts; Submit the expense report to the designated approver |

request.prompt:
Analyze the writing style of the following text samples from the same user.
These are real examples of text they produced while working.

TEXT SAMPLES:

[1] Search query: 'receipt after:{{date}}'
[2] Locate the source documents by searching the email archive; the search query varies based on the specific period of receipts being processed.
[3] File name: {{receipt_filename}}
[4] Select the relevant email thread to access the receipt details and download the necessary file for the expense record.
[5] Report name: {{report_name}}
[6] Initialize a new report container to organize the expenses found in the previous steps.
[7] Merchant: {{merchant}}, Amount: {{amount}}, Category: {{category}}, Date: {{date}}
[8] Populate the expense form with the specific transaction data extracted from the downloaded receipt.
[9] File: {{receipt_filename}}
[10] Link the physical evidence (the downloaded PDF) to the digital expense entry to validate the cost.

Respond with a JSON object describing their writing voice:

{
  "formality": "<formal | neutral | casual>",
  "tone": "<e.g. friendly, matter-of-fact, enthusiastic, dry, empathetic, professional>",
  "sentence_style": "<e.g. short and punchy, long and detailed, mixed, fragmented>",
  "vocabulary": "<e.g. simple and direct, technical, varied and rich, colloquial>",
  "personality_markers": ["<list 2-4 distinctive traits, e.g. uses humor, asks rhetorical questions, hedges with maybe/perhaps, exclamation marks, emoji>"],
  "sample_phrases": ["<2-3 short phrases that are most characteristic of their style>"],
  "would_say": "<a single example sentence this person would naturally write>",
  "would_never_say": "<a single example sentence that would feel wrong coming from this person>"
}

Rules:
- Base everything on the actual text samples, not assumptions
- If the samples are too short or generic to characterize, set tone to "insufficient_data"
- Be specific — "casual" is not enough, say "casual with dry humor and emoji"
- personality_markers should be things an agent could actually replicate

Respond with ONLY the JSON object.

response.response:
{
  "formality": "neutral",
  "tone": "matter-of-fact",
  "sentence_style": "short and punchy",
  "vocabulary": "technical",
  "personality_markers": ["uses variable placeholders like {{date}} or {{receipt_filename}}", "avoids emotional language or rhetorical questions", "prioritizes procedural clarity over engagement"],
  "sample_phrases": ["Initialize a new report container", "Link the physical evidence to the digital expense entry", "Select the relevant email thread"],
  "would_say": "Populate the expense form with the specific transaction data extracted from the downloaded receipt.",
  "would_never_say": "I hope this helps you out! 😊 Just let me know if you need any further assistance."
}

search_document: Upload receipts to expense report
Locate the source documents by searching the email archive; the search query varies based on the specific period of receipts being processed.
Select the relevant email thread to access the receipt details and download the necessary file for the expense record.
Initialize a new report container to organize the expenses found in the previous steps.
Populate the expense form with the specific transaction data extracted from the downloaded receipt.
Link the physical evidence (the downloaded PDF) to the digital expense entry to validate the cost.
